symptom: `alter page … set (eventDataAttribute: JsonData) on chart1` was refused for every spelling: "pluggable property \"eventDataAttribute\" holds a value of kind Attribute, which ALTER cannot set from a plain value — rewrite the widget with CREATE OR REPLACE PAGE (or ALTER PAGE REPLACE) instead"; `$Ctx.EventData` failed earlier, at parse, as "takes a plain value, not an expression". check --references refused the same, so one binding could only be fixed by rewriting the whole widget.
cause: Which entity a bare attribute name belongs to is the widget's binding rule applied to the property's datasource link and the scopes around it — not a fact of the BSON the page mutator holds — so setPluggableWidgetPropertyMut had nothing to qualify a name with and refused the kind outright. The ALTER SET visitor refused every expression-shaped value except DynamicClasses / DynamicCellClass, `$Param.Attr` included.
fix: The mutator reports the property instead of binding it: PluggablePropertyScope (an optional backend.PluggablePropertyScoper) gives the kind, DataSourceProperty link, and the linked and enclosing sources' entity or flow. The executor (resolvePluggableSetValue) binds by CREATE's own functions — resolveBindingScope, misboundAttributeError (CE1613 and CE7247 refusals word for word), parameterVariable for `$Param.Attr`, resolveAttributePathForEntity for inherited members — and hands the mutator a backend.AttributeBinding, which writes AttributeRef and SourceVariable (null when bound to the context object). The visitor passes the strict `$Param.Attr` shape (ast.IsParameterAttributeText) through as a WidgetExpressionV3; on any other property the executor refuses it. check dry-runs the same applySetProperties, so it follows with no code of its own.
insight: When a mutator refuses a kind because it 'cannot know' something, check whether the executor already knows it: here the whole binding rule existed for CREATE and only the property's link and scopes had to be read out of the stored document. Keep the mutator a writer of resolved values and the refusals stay shared — a second binding rule in the mutator is the duplicate-resolver drift that this area keeps paying for. The SourceVariable has to be written as null when a binding returns to the context object: leaving the stale `$Ctx` in place was measured as CE7247 "Attribute 'MyFirstModule.ChartEntry.JsonData' is not an attribute of entity 'MyFirstModule.ChartContext'" on 11.12.5, with describe printing `$Ctx.JsonData`. Wrong turn to skip: relaxing the visitor's expression refusal in general — only the one `$Param.Attr` shape is a binding.
